column1: # Written by Claude (origin "claude"). One line per entry:  entry id|typical learner mistake|usage note
# Notes are in English. Either text column may be empty.
nl:hebben:verb|Most verbs make the perfect with hebben, but movement to a place and change of state take zijn: "ik ben gegaan", "hij is gestorven".|
nl:zijn:verb||Zijn is also the auxiliary of the perfect for verbs of movement to a place and change of state: "ik ben naar huis gegaan".
nl:je:pronoun||Je is the unstressed form of jij, and also means "one, people" in general: "je weet maar nooit".
nl:er:adverb||Er has several jobs: "there" (er is een probleem), "of them" (ik heb er twee) and with prepositions (ik denk erover na).
nl:mogen:verb||Mogen means to be allowed to, and also to like someone: "ik mag hem wel".
nl:willen:verb|"Ik wil" means I want. The future is "ik zal" or, more often, "ik ga" + infinitive.|
nl:gaan:verb||Gaan + infinitive is the near future: "ik ga eten".
nl:door:preposition|Door means through, and by in the passive ("door hem geschreven"). A door is "een deur".|
nl:eens:adverb||Eens softens a request ("kijk eens"); "het eens zijn" means to agree.
nl:maar:adverb||Maar also softens an instruction: "kom maar binnen" (come on in).
nl:wel:adverb||Wel contradicts a negative or adds emphasis: "Ik ben niet moe." "Jij bent wel moe!"
nl:lekker:adjective||Lekker means tasty, but also nice or pleasant in general: "lekker weer".
nl:gezellig:adjective||There is no exact English word: cosy, sociable, a pleasant atmosphere with people.
nl:raar:adjective|Raar means strange, not rare (zeldzaam).|
nl:slim:adjective|Slim means clever, not slim (slank).|
nl:bang:adjective||Bang means afraid: "ik ben bang voor honden".
nl:bellen:verb||Bellen means to phone someone, and also to ring a bell.
nl:hoe:adverb||"Hoe gaat het?" means "How are you?"
nl:nog:adverb|"Nog niet" means not yet; "nog steeds" means still.|
nl:kennen:verb|Kennen is to know people and places, and also to know a language: "ik ken Duits". For facts use weten: "ik weet het".|
nl:weten:verb|Weten is for facts: "ik weet waar hij woont". People and places: kennen.|
